title: Automated Pull Request Code Reviewer with Prompt Injection Defense
problem: Software engineering teams face code review bottlenecks that stall delivery cycles, while automated LLM review bots frequently hallucinate non-existent issues, miss critical security vulnerabilities, and remain vulnerable to indirect prompt injection embedded within untrusted code diffs. This project builds an automated code review and security scanner bot in Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, and the GitHub API. The system parses Git pull request diffs into abstract syntax tree (AST) code chunks using Tree-sitter, sanitizes untrusted input against prompt injection attacks, prompts local or API-backed large language models to identify security vulnerabilities and design flaws, validates structured review schemas using Pydantic, and generates automated inline GitHub PR comments and SARIF vulnerability reports.
use_cases: Automated pull request gating detecting OWASP security vulnerabilities before human engineering review
Continuous integration security scanning verifying safe API usage and token handling in pull requests
Developer coaching bots delivering educational code style and performance remediation suggestions
hard_parts: Defending LLM review prompts against indirect prompt injection embedded inside submitted code comments and variable names
Extracting minimal syntactic code context around modified lines using AST parsing to stay within LLM token budgets
Enforcing strict structured JSON outputs from language models using Pydantic schemas and programmatic validation retries
Minimizing false positive review findings to prevent alert fatigue among software engineering teams
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating diff parsers, AST context extractors, prompt sanitizers, and GitHub API clients
Security evaluation benchmark verifying detection of 50 planted vulnerabilities across OWASP top categories
Anti-fake verification script submitting an adversarial PR containing prompt injection and asserting defensive interception

architecture.data_flow: GitHub pull request events trigger the FastAPI webhook endpoint; the Git Diff Extractor parses modified hunks and resolves enclosing AST function nodes; the Prompt Injection Sanitizer inspects untrusted diff text for injection tokens and wraps payloads in hardened XML delimiters; the structured review prompt dispatches to the LLM; responses are validated against Pydantic schema models; valid findings map to exact file line coordinates; the GitHub Dispatcher posts inline review comments to the PR and saves a SARIF artifact.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Pydantic schema validation rejecting malformed LLM outputs; hardened prompt delimiters isolating untrusted diff content.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an automated GitHub PR code review bot in Python/FastAPI with Pydantic structured output, Tree-sitter AST context, and prompt injection defense.
worksheet.q2: Target users: AI platform engineers, developer tooling teams, and security platform engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: automated PR security gating, CI/CD code compliance scanning, and developer coaching.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: prompt injection defense in untrusted diffs, AST minimal context slicing, Pydantic structured output enforcement, and false-positive reduction.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50 PR diffs totaling 8,000 LOC with seeded vulnerabilities and injection payloads. Permissive open-source code only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, free GitHub PAT. Fallback: deterministic mock LLM provider.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Non-deterministic LLM JSON outputs. Fallback: JSON repair parser and schema correction loop.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static review comments. Anti-fake check 5 injects adversarial instruction at runtime and asserts INJECTION_DETECTED flag.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; static diff analysis only, no code execution.
